To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lived experience of fathering a child with asthma is one of relief, learning, vigilance, concern, and management.
fathers who have children who have asthma feel relief in knowing the asthma diagnosis, learn to be vigilant, live with concern, and are comfortable managing the asthma.

fathers of children with asthma experience relief in knowing the asthma diagnosis, learn the ropes of asthma management and feel vigilant about asthma management, live with concern about their children's health and well-being and feel comfortable with the asthma management.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the father-child relationship, and how fathers experience the diagnosis and management of asthma in children.
the experience of fathers in caring for a school-age child with asthma.

the lived experience of being the father of a child with asthma is characterized by a complex interplay of feelings of relief, learning the ropes and being vigilant, living in concern and comfort with asthma management.
fathers of children with asthma have a unique lived experience.

fathers of children who have asthma are vigilant, concerned and comfortable in their role as caregivers.
fathers of children with asthma are relieved that they have a diagnosis, but they also experience concern and uncertainty.
